subject: general
question: In December 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru, president of Indian National Congress, formally demanded __________ from British Government.
solution:
The correct answer is __**complete freedom**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In December 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru, as the president of the Indian National Congress, formally demanded **complete freedom** from the British Government.
 
• This demand marked a significant shift from the previous demand for dominion status to the more radical goal of complete independence.
 
• The resolution for complete freedom was passed during the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in 1929.
 
• This session is also notable for the declaration of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as the ultimate goal of the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• The Indian National Congress decided to observe 26th January 1930 as Independence Day, which later became the date when the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The demand for complete freedom was a turning point in the Indian freedom struggle, galvanizing the Indian populace and intensifying the fight against British colonial rule.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru's leadership during this period played a crucial role in uniting various factions within the Congress and presenting a united front against the British.
 
• The Lahore session also saw the adoption of the tricolor as the national flag of India.
 
• This period marked the beginning of a series of civil disobedience movements and protests that eventually led to India gaining independence in 1947.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru later became the first Prime Minister of independent India, serving from 1947 until his death in 1964.
